term: Why use csv.DictReader instead of csv.reader?
meaning: Because DictReader automatically turns each row into a dictionary using the header names as keys

term: Why store each term as a dictionary?
meaning: So that one item can hold multiple related pieces of information (type term meaning category)

term: Why put all terms into a list of dictionaries?
meaning: So the program can easily loop through them select random ones and filter by type

term: Why use a separate terms.csv file?
meaning: To separate data from logic so terms can be updated without touching the Python code

term: Why not hard-code the terms inside quiz.py?
meaning: Hard-coding makes the file long hard to maintain and difficult for non-programmers to update

term: Why use functions for almost everything?
meaning: To make the code organized reusable easier to test and easier to understand

term: Why use while True for the main menu?
meaning: So the program keeps running until the user deliberately chooses to exit

term: Why use try-except when asking for number of questions?
meaning: To prevent the program from crashing if the user types text instead of a number

term: Why track recently asked questions?
meaning: To reduce repetition and make the quiz feel less predictable

term: Why save progress in JSON instead of CSV?
meaning: JSON is better for nested structured data like lists of wrong answers and review dates

term: Why use random.sample instead of random.choice in a loop?
meaning: random.sample guarantees unique questions in one quiz round

term: Why make is_correct() a separate function?
meaning: So the same answer-checking logic can be reused in quiz reverse practice and spaced repetition

term: Why allow flexible answer checking instead of exact match?
meaning: Because students may write partially correct answers and strict matching would be too frustrating

term: Why start with a CLI version?
meaning: It is simpler to build test and debug while learning the core logic

term: Why keep main branch as the stable version?
meaning: So users always get the best working code when they clone the repository

term: Why use a feature branch for big changes?
meaning: To protect the working version and experiment safely

term: Why use a Personal Access Token?
meaning: GitHub no longer accepts account passwords for Git operations and tokens are safer

term: Why make the repository public later and not immediately?
meaning: So you can improve the README and code quality before showing it to the world

term: Why create a separate Active Recall trainer project?
meaning: So it can grow independently and serve as a learning tool without mixing with the main project

term: Why use clear() function?
meaning: To improve user experience by cleaning the screen between different sections

term: Why load the CSV only once at the start?
meaning: To avoid reading the file repeatedly which would be slower and unnecessary

term: Why store wrong answers with a future review time?
meaning: To implement basic spaced repetition so difficult items appear again later

term: Separation of Concerns
meaning: Keeping different responsibilities (data vs logic) in different places

term: Single Responsibility
meaning: Each function should do one clear thing

term: Data Structure Choice
meaning: Choosing list of dictionaries because each term has multiple attributes

term: Control Flow
meaning: Using while True + if-elif to control the program menu

term: Error Prevention
meaning: Using try-except and checks to stop the program from crashing

term: Persistence
meaning: Saving data to JSON so progress survives after the program closes

term: What is the purpose of the load_terms() function?
meaning: To read the CSV file and convert it into a list of dictionaries the rest of the program can use

term: What would break if you remove the header row from terms.csv?
meaning: csv.DictReader would not know the column names and the program would fail or behave incorrectly

term: Why do we check len(user) < 3 in is_correct()?
meaning: To reject very short or empty answers that are almost certainly wrong

term: What is the danger of working directly on the main branch?
meaning: You can easily break the stable version of the project

term: Why should commit messages be clear and professional?
meaning: Because they become part of the public history of the project

term: What is the benefit of a good README?
meaning: It helps other people understand and use your project quickly

term: Why is medical terminology a good project domain?
meaning: It has clear structure (prefix + root + suffix) and real educational value

term: What is the biggest limitation of the current Medical Terminology Assistant?
meaning: It is still command-line only and not user-friendly for non-technical medical students

term: How does the program know which questions are due for spaced repetition?
meaning: It compares the saved next_review time with the current time

term: Main challenge when connecting CSV to Python
meaning: Making sure the code remains flexible when the CSV content changes

term: Why was answer checking difficult to get right?
meaning: Because too loose checking accepts wrong answers and too strict checking frustrates users

term: Why prefer CSV over SQLite in the first version?
meaning: CSV is simpler to edit and sufficient for learning and small data

term: When should you move from CSV to SQLite?
meaning: When the data becomes large or you need more advanced querying and relationships

term: Active Recall Trainer Purpose
meaning: To force deep understanding of every decision and concept used in the project

term: Systems Thinking in this project
meaning: Understanding how data logic user experience and learning science work together
